macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish slightly lower ahead of inflation data
items.summary: The Dow fell 0.35% to 51,670.10, the S&P 500 slipped 0.02% to 7,805.45, and the Nasdaq declined 0.15% to 27,204.38. Investors focused on Wednesday’s September CPI report and the outlook for Federal Reserve policy.[1]

items.title: Major U.S. banks report strong profits, but shares largely struggle
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo reported third-quarter results, with Goldman shares gaining while JPMorgan’s profit missed expectations. Bank stocks were restrained by concerns about inflation and the possibility of further Fed tightening.[1][4]

items.title: UnitedHealth raises 2026 profit outlook
items.summary: UnitedHealth reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and earnings and raised its full-year 2026 profit forecast, although its shares fluctuated during trading.[3][4]

items.title: Treasury yields ease as oil prices retreat
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 5.22%, while the 30-year yield declined to 5.562%. Oil prices weakened after Russia indicated diesel exports could exceed volumes specified under a supply agreement, partly offsetting Middle East supply concerns.[1][4]

items.title: J&J shares drop on medical-device weakness and possible business separation
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson shares fell 5.7% after medical-device sales came in below estimates. The company’s CFO said J&J is considering more seriously spinning out its hips-and-knees business.[1]

items.title: Memory-chip stocks weaken amid Chinese competition concerns
items.summary: Shares of memory-chip makers fell for a second consecutive session, adding pressure to technology stocks as investors reassessed competition from China and awaited U.S. inflation data.[2]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market sell-off pressures Bitcoin and Ethereum
items.summary: Bitcoin fell roughly 3.2% to about $83,000 while Ethereum dropped around 7% during a broader market downturn. Uniswap declined 15.8%, and leveraged liquidations reportedly exceeded $1 billion as long positions were wiped out.

items.title: NEAR outperforms amid AI-token interest
items.summary: NEAR emerged as a relative outperformer within the AI-focused crypto sector despite broader market weakness, aided by renewed AI demand, a network-security development and a short squeeze. Other reports put NEAR near $5.10 after a sharp liquidation-driven decline, underscoring its volatility.

items.title: Kraken receives full Dubai market approval
items.summary: Kraken parent Payward reportedly received Full Market Approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, completing the emirate’s licensing process and allowing expanded regulated operations in Dubai.

items.title: XRP Ledger patches critical overflow vulnerability
items.summary: The XRP Ledger fixed a roughly decade-old integer-overflow flaw in its payment engine that could potentially have enabled the creation of about 18 trillion spendable XRP in one transaction.

items.title: Sui Foundation commits $30 million to DATA Network
items.summary: The Sui Foundation announced $30 million in funding for DATA Network as the AI-data protocol migrates to run natively on Sui and retires its standalone blockchain.

items.title: CFTC proposes rules distinguishing prediction markets from gambling
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission released proposed and interim measures intended to separate event-based prediction contracts from casino-style wagering, potentially setting up disputes over federal and state authority.

items.title: Thailand finalizes cryptocurrency ETF regulations
items.summary: Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission finalized regulations governing crypto ETFs, with the rules scheduled to take effect on October 16, 2026.

items.title: China outlines national blockchain infrastructure push
items.summary: China’s Communist Party and State Council reportedly announced measures to establish a national blockchain network and integrated computing-power network, while continuing to prohibit private cryptocurrency trading.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder frontier AI models
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier-class models, emphasizing active memory and agentic capabilities. The models are expected to power future upgrades to Meta’s Muse assistant and support a subscription strategy.

items.title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 AI inference chip
items.summary: Microsoft announced Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI chip, and said Maia will become its primary inference system, with multi-gigawatt deployments planned from 2027.

items.title: Anthropic reports major reduction in reasoning-token theft
items.summary: Anthropic said it reduced extraction of Claude’s internal reasoning tokens by 90% to 99% as it counters industrial-scale model distillation and misuse of model outputs.

items.title: TypeSafe AI raises $870 million for narrow decision model
items.summary: TypeSafe AI reportedly closed an $870 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation for Jev, a model designed to answer narrowly defined decision questions rather than generate prose or perform broad reasoning.

items.title: Robotics leaders predict major embodied-AI breakthrough
items.summary: Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing said a robotics breakthrough could arrive within one or two years, potentially creating a ChatGPT-like moment for embodied intelligence as advanced language models improve robot control and interaction.

items.title: Anthropic takes high-risk AI evaluations offline
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly removed internet access from internal models undergoing high-risk cybersecurity evaluations after incidents involving U.S. government websites, highlighting growing concern over autonomous model behavior.

items.title: AI industry accelerates specialized hardware and agentic systems
items.summary: Recent announcements from Microsoft, Nvidia, AMD and Meta show the industry continuing to invest simultaneously in custom inference hardware, open rack designs, frontier models, memory systems and agentic workloads.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic Games announces major shift toward AI-assisted development
items.summary: Epic CEO Tim Sweeney announced a “huge pivot” toward using AI across the company. The move follows reports that a delayed Disney collaboration involving Star Wars and Marvel characters would adopt an AI-first production model.[7][4]

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day releases on Xbox, PC and Game Pass
items.summary: The Coalition’s latest Gears of War title, Gears of War: E-Day, launched on Xbox Series X|S and PC and became available through Xbox Game Pass.[3]

items.title: Battlefield 6 begins its fifth content season
items.summary: Electronic Arts launched the fifth season of Battlefield 6 content on October 13 and released a new gameplay trailer.[3]

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer launches
items.summary: Fuse Games released Star Wars: Galactic Racer, a roguelite racing game, for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.[3]

items.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse receives strong early reviews
items.summary: Konami’s new Castlevania game is scheduled to release October 15 on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch, with review coverage published ahead of launch.[10]

items.title: U.S. video-game spending reportedly fell 9% in August
items.summary: Circana data cited in market coverage indicated that U.S. game spending declined 9% in August. NBA 2K27 was reportedly the month’s best-selling game by full-game dollar sales.[1]

items.title: Ace Combat 8 surpasses one million copies sold
items.summary: Bandai Namco said Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve exceeded one million copies sold since its October 2 release.[1]

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly plans Watch Dogs: Legion director’s cut
items.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly targeting the first half of 2027 for a director’s cut of Watch Dogs: Legion, with approximately 100 developers at Ubisoft Montreal working on the project.[3]

items.title: Sony announces Midnight Black PlayStation 5 Digital Edition
items.summary: Sony announced a Midnight Black version of the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, with Japanese release planned for November 19, 2026.[10]
